Council Approves Night Ferry Pilot & New Dock Fees

By Marta Ilves — October 12, 2026

The city council voted 7–2 on Tuesday to fund a six-month night ferry pilot, ending a debate that has run since spring. Supporters said late-shift workers on the north shore have waited years for a reliable crossing, while opponents worried about noise near the residential piers.

Under the plan, a single boat will run every forty minutes between 11 p.m. and 4 a.m., stopping at Pier 3 and the Linden Street landing. The pilot will cost roughly $860,000, most of which will come from a new fee on private dock moorings, according to the city’s budget office.

“People who clean our hospitals and bake our bread deserve a way home,” said council member Ruth Okafor, who sponsored the measure. She added that ridership will be counted nightly, and that the council can end the pilot early if fewer than ninety people use it on an average night.

Dock owners pushed back during public comment, arguing that the fee falls hardest on small marinas rather than on commercial operators. Several speakers asked the council to phase the fee in over two years, but an amendment to do so failed on a 4–5 vote.

The first sailing is scheduled for January 6. Riders will pay the standard transit fare, and monthly passes will be accepted, the transit authority said in a statement posted to its website.
